name: Alabama

creditorClaims.text: Claims must be filed in the probate office within 6 months after the grant of letters or 5 months after the first publication of notice, whichever is later; creditors entitled to actual notice have 30 days after notice; unfiled claims are forever barred (Ala. Code § 43-2-350).

earliestClose.text: No specific minimum is stated; distribution and final settlement follow the 6-month claims period of Ala. Code § 43-2-350, and executors must make annual settlements meanwhile (Ala. Code § 43-2-500).

smallEstate.text: Summary distribution without a personal representative by verified petition to the probate judge for a 'small estate' (personal property only, decedent owning no real property) whose value does not exceed the small estate amount, defined as the sum of the homestead allowance, exempt property and family allowance as adjusted every 3 years for inflation by the State Treasurer (Ala. Code §§ 43-2-691, 43-2-692, 43-8-116; Revised Alabama Small Estates Act, Act 2025-431).

simplified.text: Summary distribution of a small estate by petition to the judge of probate, with one published notice and notice to the Alabama Medicaid Agency (Ala. Code § 43-2-692, as revised by Act 2025-431).

filingFee.text: Judge of probate statutory fee of $45.00 for probate of a will (up to 5 pages, with 3 certified copies of letters and final settlement up to 10 pages) or grant of letters of administration (Ala. Code § 12-19-90(a)(1),(2)); counties may add other fees.

personalRepFee.text: Reasonable compensation fixed by the court considering listed factors, not exceeding 2.5% of the value of all property received and under the personal representative's control plus 2.5% of all disbursements; extra for extraordinary services (Ala. Code § 43-2-848).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the court fixes and allows the attorney's fee or compensation paid from the estate at each annual, partial or final settlement (Ala. Code § 43-2-682).

name: Alaska

creditorClaims.text: Pre-death claims are barred unless presented within 4 months after the first publication of notice to creditors, or within 3 years after death if notice was not published (AS 13.16.460(a)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, stating that notice to creditors was first published more than 6 months earlier (AS 13.16.630).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, consists only of personal property not exceeding $50,000 plus registered vehicles with a total value not exceeding $100,000, and no personal representative application is pending (AS 13.16.680). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary administration: if the estate does not exceed family allowances, exempt property, administration costs, funeral and last-illness expenses, the personal representative may distribute and close at any time by verified statement (AS 13.16.690, 13.16.695).

filingFee.text: Superior court filing fee of $250.00 upon filing a trust or estate action other than registration or deposit of a will (Alaska Administrative Rule 9(b)(2)(A)).

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (AS 13.16.430), reviewable by the court (AS 13.16.440).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of any attorney employed by the personal representative (AS 13.16.440); reasonable attorney fees in good-faith estate litigation are paid from the estate (AS 13.16.435).

name: Arizona

creditorClaims.text: The personal representative publishes notice once a week for 3 weeks; claims must be presented within 4 months after first publication, or for known creditors given written notice within the later of that period or 60 days after mailing (A.R.S. § 14-3801). Pre-death claims are in any event barred 2 years after death plus any remaining notice period (A.R.S. § 14-3803).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, a personal representative may close the estate by sworn closing statement no earlier than 4 months after the original appointment of a general personal representative, after determining that the claims period has expired (A.R.S. § 14-3933).

smallEstate.text: Thirty days after death, successors may collect personal property by affidavit if no personal representative has been appointed and all personal property, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $200,000 (A.R.S. § 14-3971(B)); real property in Arizona up to $300,000 net of liens (assessed full cash value) can pass by affidavit of succession filed with the court no sooner than 6 months after death (A.R.S. § 14-3971(E)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Informal probate and appointment before the registrar (A.R.S. Title 14, ch. 3, art. 3) and closing by sworn statement 4 months after appointment (A.R.S. § 14-3933); affidavit collection for personal property up to $200,000 and affidavit of succession for real property up to $300,000 (A.R.S. § 14-3971).

filingFee.text: Statutory clerk fee of $149.00 for an application for informal probate or appointment, or a petition in formal testacy or appointment proceedings (A.R.S. § 12-284(A), class C); statutory surcharges and local fees may be added by the clerk.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation (A.R.S. § 14-3719); the court may review its reasonableness on petition (A.R.S. § 14-3721).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule: the estate pays reasonable attorneys' fees (A.R.S. § 14-3720), which the court may review (A.R.S. § 14-3721); fiduciaries and their attorneys must manage costs prudently (A.R.S. § 14-1104).

name: California

creditorClaims.text: A creditor must file a claim before the later of 4 months after letters are first issued to a general personal representative or 60 days after notice of administration is mailed or delivered to the creditor (Prob. Code § 9100); this does not extend the 1-year limit of Code Civ. Proc. § 366.2.

earliestClose.text: No final distribution before the 4-month creditor claim period of Prob. Code § 9100 has run; the inventory and appraisal is due within 4 months after letters (Prob. Code § 8800).

smallEstate.text: Affidavit collection of personal property without probate if the gross value of the decedent's California real and personal property (excluding property described in § 13050, such as joint tenancy, trust and spousal property, and property in a § 13151 petition) does not exceed $208,850 for deaths on or after April 1, 2025 ($184,500 for deaths April 1, 2022 to March 31, 2025), and 40 days have elapsed since death (Prob. Code §§ 13100, 13101). The amount is adjusted every 3 years by the Judicial Council (Prob. Code § 890); next adjustment April 1, 2028 (form DE-300).

simplified.text: For deaths on or after April 1, 2025: court order determining succession to a primary residence worth up to $750,000 (Prob. Code § 13151); affidavit for real property of small value up to $69,625 (Prob. Code § 13200); small estate set-aside for spouse and minor children up to $107,900 net (Prob. Code §§ 6602, 6609); otherwise full probate, often with independent administration (Prob. Code § 10400 et seq.). Amounts from Judicial Council form DE-300 (rev. April 28, 2025).

filingFee.text: First-filed petition for letters of administration or letters testamentary: $435 (Gov. Code § 70650(a)), Statewide Civil Fee Schedule effective January 1, 2026, row 124; some counties add local surcharges (asterisk in schedule).

personalRepFee.text: Statutory compensation for ordinary services based on the estate accounted for (inventory value plus gains on sales plus receipts, less losses, without deducting encumbrances): 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, 1% of the next $9,000,000, 0.5% of the next $15,000,000, and a reasonable amount set by the court above $25,000,000 (Prob. Code § 10800).

attorneyFee.text: The attorney for the personal representative receives the same statutory percentages as the personal representative for ordinary services: 4% / 3% / 2% / 1% / 0.5%, court-set above $25,000,000 (Prob. Code § 10810).

name: Colorado

creditorClaims.text: The published notice sets a claims date not earlier than 4 months after first publication (or 1 year after death if earlier) (C.R.S. 15-12-801); claims are barred after that date, after the date in a written notice, and in all cases 1 year after death (C.R.S. 15-12-803(1)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, an estate may be closed by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment or 1 year after death, whichever occurs first (C.R.S. 15-12-1003(1)).

smallEstate.text: Ten days after death, successors may collect property by affidavit if the decedent's property subject to will or intestacy, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed twice the exempt-property amount of C.R.S. 15-11-403 as adjusted by C.R.S. 15-10-112 (C.R.S. 15-12-1201(1)(a)). The $30,000 exempt amount is increased by the CPI-U change since 2010, rounded down to $1,000: for deaths in 2026, 30,000 x (321.943 / 218.056 - 1) = 14,292.70, rounded down to 14,000, so $44,000 exempt property and an affidavit limit of $88,000 (computed).

simplified.text: Affidavit collection (C.R.S. 15-12-1201); summary administration when the estate does not exceed fiduciary property, allowances, administration, funeral and last-illness expenses (C.R.S. 15-12-1203); closing by sworn statement (C.R.S. 15-12-1003).

filingFee.text: Probate filing fees are set in C.R.S. Title 13 (not read).

personalRepFee.text: A fiduciary and its lawyer are entitled to reasonable compensation (C.R.S. 15-10-602(1)), judged under the factors of C.R.S. 15-10-603; the former UPC § 3-719 (C.R.S. 15-12-719) was repealed in 2011.

attorneyFee.text: The fiduciary's lawyer is entitled to reasonable compensation (C.R.S. 15-10-602(1)); no method of charging is presumed unreasonable (C.R.S. 15-10-603(2)).

name: Connecticut

creditorClaims.text: Connecticut has no general claims bar date: a fiduciary who pays or distributes in good faith is not chargeable for claims presented more than 150 days after appointment of the first fiduciary (C.G.S. § 45a-356); the fiduciary may give optional notice barring a claim not presented by a date at least 90 days after the notice (C.G.S. § 45a-357); all claims are limited to 2 years after death (C.G.S. § 45a-375(c)).

earliestClose.text: No statutory minimum; distribution is protected after the 150-day period following appointment of the first fiduciary (C.G.S. § 45a-356).

smallEstate.text: Small estate affidavit filed in the Probate Court instead of probate when the decedent's solely owned personal property (excluding property passing outside probate) does not exceed $40,000 and the decedent owned no solely owned Connecticut real property; the court issues a decree no earlier than 30 days after sending the affidavit to the Department of Administrative Services (C.G.S. § 45a-273). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Settlement of small estates by affidavit and Probate Court decree for personal property up to $40,000 with no solely owned real property (C.G.S. § 45a-273).

filingFee.text: For deaths on or after July 1, 2016 the Probate Court fee depends on the basis (greatest of inventory, succession/estate tax gross estate or Connecticut taxable estate; property passing to a surviving spouse counted at 50%): $25 up to $500; $50 up to $1,000; $50 + 1% of excess over $1,000 up to $10,000; $150 + 0.35% over $10,000 up to $500,000; $1,865 + 0.25% over $500,000 up to $2,000,000; $5,615 + 0.5% over $2,000,000 up to $8,877,000; $40,000 cap above; minimum $150 if a full estate is opened with a basis under $10,000 (C.G.S. § 45a-107(b)). The amount is value-based and is computed from the court-fee schedule in fees/connecticut.json (filingFee.amount left null to avoid double counting).

name: Florida

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless filed by the later of 3 months after the first publication of the notice to creditors or, for creditors who must be served, 30 days after service (Fla. Stat. § 733.702); all claims are barred 2 years after death whether or not letters issued (Fla. Stat. § 733.710).

earliestClose.text: The estate cannot be closed before the 3-month creditor period after first publication of the notice to creditors has run and timely claims are resolved (Fla. Stat. § 733.702); after administration is completed the personal representative is discharged (Fla. Stat. § 733.901).

smallEstate.text: Florida has no small-estate affidavit; the simplified route is summary administration, available if the estate subject to administration in Florida, less exempt property, does not exceed $150,000 (raised from $75,000 by ch. 2026-57, effective July 1, 2026) or the decedent has been dead more than 2 years, and the will does not direct formal administration (Fla. Stat. § 735.201). The amount is not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary administration for estates up to $150,000 net of exempt property or deaths more than 2 years ago (Fla. Stat. § 735.201); disposition without administration by court letter when the estate is only exempt property plus non-exempt personal property not exceeding preferred funeral expenses and last-60-days medical expenses (Fla. Stat. § 735.301).

filingFee.text: Clerk fee for formal administration: up to $395; summary administration $340 (estates of $1,000 or more) or $230 (under $1,000); disposition of personal property without administration $230; plus a $4 service charge on petitions for summary or formal administration (Fla. Stat. § 28.2401(1),(3)).

personalRepFee.text: Commission presumed reasonable in formal administration, on the inventory value of probate assets plus income earned during administration: 3% of the first $1 million, 2.5% from $1 million to $5 million, 2% from $5 million to $10 million, 1.5% above $10 million, plus reasonable compensation for extraordinary services (Fla. Stat. § 733.617).

attorneyFee.text: Attorneys receive reasonable compensation; a fee is presumed reasonable in formal administration if based on the compensable value: $1,500 up to $40,000, $2,250 up to $70,000, $3,000 up to $100,000, then 3% on the next $900,000, 2.5% from $1 million to $3 million, 2% from $3 million to $5 million, 1.5% from $5 million to $10 million, 1% above $10 million, plus extraordinary services; written disclosures are required to use the schedule (Fla. Stat. § 733.6171).

name: Iowa

creditorClaims.text: Claims are barred unless filed with the clerk within the later of 4 months after the second publication of the notice to creditors or, for reasonably ascertainable creditors, 1 month after notice is mailed (Iowa Code § 633.410).

earliestClose.text: Final settlement must be made within 3 years after the second publication of the notice to creditors unless the court orders otherwise (Iowa Code § 633.473); no earlier date is fixed beyond the 4-month claims bar of § 633.410.

smallEstate.text: Forty days after death, a successor may collect personal property by affidavit if the decedent's entire probate estate (excluding the surviving spouse's or domestic partner's community share), less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative application is pending (RCW 11.62.010). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit procedure up to $100,000 (RCW 11.62.010); nonintervention probate closed by declaration of completion without court approval (RCW 11.68.110).

filingFee.text: In probate proceedings the party instituting them pays $200 when filing the first document (RCW 36.18.020(2)(f)); counties may add local surcharges.

personalRepFee.text: Absent a will provision, the personal representative receives compensation the court deems just and reasonable (RCW 11.48.210).

attorneyFee.text: An attorney performing services for the estate receives compensation the court deems just and reasonable (RCW 11.48.210); fees paid must be disclosed in the declaration of completion (RCW 11.68.110).

uncertain: Effective date of the $100,000 affidavit limit not shown (smallEstate.effective = null).

name: West Virginia

creditorClaims.text: The fiduciary supervisor publishes a monthly notice; claims must be exhibited to the fiduciary or the fiduciary supervisor within 60 days of the first publication of the notice, otherwise they may be excluded from the estate (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-4). The period is 60 days, not a whole number of months.

earliestClose.text: Once more than 60 days have elapsed since the notice under § 44-3A-4, the estate may be closed by short form settlement with a fiduciary affidavit and beneficiary waivers (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-4a).

smallEstate.text: Estates whose appraised assets subject to administration (excluding real estate unless the will requires its administration) total $100,000 or less are not referred to a fiduciary commissioner and are settled under the fiduciary supervisor (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-5). West Virginia has no small-estate affidavit in the sections read. Not indexed.

simplified.text: Supervision by the county fiduciary supervisor without reference to a commissioner for estates of $100,000 or less (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-5) and short form settlement after 60 days (§ 44-3A-4a).

filingFee.text: County clerk probate fees were not identified in the text read.

personalRepFee.text: Commissions on personal estate subject to administration (with its income) received and accounted for and on proceeds of real estate sold: 5% of the first $100,000, 4% from $100,000 to $400,000, 3% from $400,000 to $800,000, 2% above $800,000; plus 1% of unsold real estate and of non-probate property includable for federal estate tax (not joint and survivorship property); full compensation for ordinary services, adjustable by the county commission; a will may deviate (W. Va. Code § 44-4-12a).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule; a lawyer serving as personal representative may not receive professional fees in addition to the commission (W. Va. Code § 44-4-12a(e)); other attorney fees are reasonable expenses allowed by the fiduciary commissioner (W. Va. Code § 44-4-12).

uncertain: creditorClaims.months = null because the period is 60 days (W. Va. Code § 44-3A-4).
No small-estate affidavit or probate filing fee section was read; smallEstate.limit reflects the $100,000 supervision threshold of § 44-3A-5.

name: Wisconsin

creditorClaims.text: When administration is applied for, the court or probate registrar sets a claims deadline not less than 3 nor more than 4 months from the date of the order (Wis. Stat. § 859.01); claims not filed by that date are barred (Wis. Stat. § 859.02).

earliestClose.text: Not verified: informal estates close by sworn statement (Wis. Stat. § 865.16, not read) after the 3-4 month claims deadline of § 859.01.

smallEstate.text: Transfer by affidavit when the decedent's property subject to administration in Wisconsin does not exceed $50,000 in gross value, by an heir, trustee of the decedent's revocable trust, named personal representative or former guardian (Wis. Stat. § 867.03(1g)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Summary settlement when the estate does not exceed allowances and preferred claims, or $50,000 with a surviving spouse/domestic partner or minor children (Wis. Stat. § 867.01); summary assignment up to $50,000 subject to creditors (Wis. Stat. § 867.02); informal administration (ch. 865).

filingFee.text: Probate fees are set by Wis. Stat. § 814.66 (not read).

personalRepFee.text: Subject to court approval, commissions of 2% of the inventory value of property accounted for, less mortgages or liens, plus net principal gains, or another rate agreed in writing with the decedent or majority beneficiaries, plus reasonable sums for unusual difficulty or extraordinary services (Wis. Stat. § 857.05(2)).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory attorney schedule; a personal representative who also serves as estate attorney receives either executor commissions or attorney fees as the court allows (Wis. Stat. § 857.05(3)).

uncertain: docs.legis.wisconsin.gov refuses connections from this environment: Wis. Stat. ch. 859 (snapshot 2025-12-14), ch. 857 (2025-08-07), ch. 865 (2026-02-18), ch. 867 (2026-10-05) and § 867.03 (2026-06-02) were read from Internet Archive copies of the official pages.
creditorClaims.months = null because the court sets a deadline of 3 to 4 months (§ 859.01).
Wis. Stat. § 814.66 (probate fees) not read.

name: Wyoming

creditorClaims.text: Claims must be filed with the clerk within the time in the notice to creditors; a claimant mailed a notice must file within 3 months after first publication or 30 days after mailing, whichever is later, or the claim is barred forever (W.S. 2-7-703(a)).

earliestClose.text: The estate closes by final decree of distribution after court approval of the final report and accounting (W.S. 2-7-813), which follows the 3-month claims period of W.S. 2-7-703; no other minimum period is stated.

smallEstate.text: Not earlier than 30 days after death, distributees may collect personal property by affidavit (filed with the clerk) if the entire Wyoming estate subject to administration, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $400,000 and no personal representative application is pending (W.S. 2-1-201(a)). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Decree of summary distribution of personal or real property (including minerals) on application filed at least 30 days after death when the entire estate, less liens, does not exceed $400,000, with 2 weeks' published notice (W.S. 2-1-205).

filingFee.text: The district court clerk charges an original filing fee of $160.00 for civil matters (W.S. 5-3-206(a)(i)); whether and how this applies to probate petitions was not confirmed.

personalRepFee.text: Fees for ordinary services computed on the probate estate accounted for: 10% of the first $1,000, 5% from $1,000 to $5,000, 3% from $5,000 to $20,000, 2% above $20,000; the court may allow more for unusual circumstances and extraordinary services (W.S. 2-7-803).

attorneyFee.text: Attorney for the estate: same schedule as the personal representative (10% / 5% / 3% / 2%) on the probate estate accounted for, plus extraordinary services; lower fees may be negotiated (W.S. 2-7-804).

uncertain: Wyoming statutes read from the official compiled Title 2 PDF (wyoleg.gov, last modified 2026-05-08); the effective date of the $400,000 limit in W.S. 2-1-201/2-1-205 is not shown there (smallEstate.effective = null).
Probate filing fee not confirmed: W.S. 5-3-206(a)(i) sets $160.00 for civil matters; filingFee.amount = null.
